access.title: MCP access
access.descriptionPre: Controls which MCP commands the AI agent may invoke. Disabled commands return a “disabled in panel” notice to the agent and have no effect on the engine. Commands marked
access.descriptionPost: grant the agent write access and require explicit confirmation to enable. The MCP endpoint is served at

columnDescriptions.on: This column shows whether the MCP command is currently enabled.
columnDescriptions.command: This column shows the MCP command name exposed to the agent.
columnDescriptions.description: This column explains what the command lets the agent do.
columnDescriptions.flags: This column shows safety and implementation flags for the command.

table.disabledNotice: Disabled — returns a “disabled in panel” notice to the agent.

dialog.title: Enable protected command?
dialog.body1Post: . Enabling it grants the AI agent the ability to change the database in ways the operator cannot supervise or control in real time.
dialog.body2: This is a protective barrier against autonomous AI actions. Only enable it if you intend to grant the agent that power and accept the associated risk.

health.description: Report Pit Officer deployment health (engine version/profile/liveness, store reachability).

get_account_state.description: Read an account row and its account-scoped risk barriers.

get_limits.description: List configured risk barriers, optionally filtered by account.

check_order.description: Run a non-mutating pre-trade dry-run for an order (pass/reject + reasons); changes no state.

set_limit.description: Create or change a risk-limit / policy barrier.

submit_order.description: Submit an order intent through pre-trade and obtain a signed approval token.

confirm_execution.description: Confirm execution (commit) of a previously approved order.

cancel.description: Cancel / revoke a pending approval token or reservation.

get_next_token.description: Fetch the next approval token for a trade from the registry.

report_fill.description: Report an execution fill to the engine (post-trade).

claude.cliLabel: Add the connector with the Claude CLI

chatgpt.step1: Open your custom GPT or ChatGPT connector settings.
chatgpt.step2: Add an MCP connector pointing at the URL above.

chatgpt.publicUrlCaveat: Hosted ChatGPT can only reach a publicly resolvable HTTPS URL. A loopback or localhost Officer is not reachable — expose the service on a public HTTPS endpoint first.

prompt.intro:
You have access to the Pit Officer MCP server - a pre-trade risk and
compliance control plane for trading operations.

Transport: streamable HTTP at the /mcp endpoint of this service.
Alternatively available as `pit-officer mcp` over stdio.

Principles:
- Least-privilege surface. The server carries no secrets or credentials.
- Most tools are read-only. Treat any mutating tool with extra care.
- Any trading action or mutation must go through pre-trade checks and
  approval tokens. Never bypass the pre-trade step.
prompt.discover:
Discover the available commands at runtime: call the MCP tool list
(`tools/list`) after connecting and rely on each tool's self-described
input schema. Do not assume a fixed set of commands - the surface is
self-describing and can change as the operator adjusts access.
prompt.footer:
The operator controls which commands are enabled, and this can change at
any time without notice. If a tool call returns a notice that the command
is disabled in the panel, do NOT retry it — ask your orchestrator to
extend or change your prompt/instructions accordingly (or to have the
operator enable the command in Pit Officer).
